[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with 3 bidders and i.i.d. private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: bidding higher risks negative payoff if you win at a price above your value; bidding lower risks losing when you would have gained. With value 15, bid 15. You win only if both rivals bid below 15, and pay the second-highest bid (≤14.9), guaranteeing nonnegative surplus. There is no past history to exploit and only one round, so no dynamic considerations. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. With v = 49 (top of the range), bidding 49 maximizes expected profit: it ensures winning whenever opponents’ highest bid is below 49 and you pay that second-highest bid, yielding profit v − price. Overbidding offers no gain and risks loss if rules deviate; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Bids are in 0.1 increments; 49.0 is feasible. No history to adjust for, so follow the dominant strategy. ]
